Task: Compose a detailed plan for organizing a five-day road trip across California.

Below is a thorough, ready-to-use five-day California road-trip plan, covering daily routes, lodging ideas, meal stops, budgeting guidance, key reservations, back-up options, and practical tips. Feel free to adapt distances or attractions to match your interests, season, and starting city.

────────────────────────────────
TRIP OVERVIEW
────────────────────────────────
• Theme: Classic “Pacific & Peaks” loop—coast, redwoods, wine country, Sierra foothills, and iconic national parks.  
• Duration: 5 full days / 4 nights (≈1,050 mi total; 3–4 hr average daily drive blocks).  
• Ideal months: April–June or September–October (good weather, thinner crowds).  
• Vehicle: Mid-size sedan or compact SUV; reserve early if renting.  
• Start/Finish: San Francisco (easy arrivals, one-way loops possible).

────────────────────────────────
PRE-TRIP CHECKLIST
────────────────────────────────
1. Book flights ✈️  
2. Reserve rental car with unlimited miles & toll transponder.  
3. Secure lodging (mix of hotels, Airbnbs, and one national-park stay).  
4. Buy timed-entry tickets: Yosemite (if applicable), Hearst Castle, Alcatraz.  
5. Purchase America the Beautiful annual park pass ($80); pays for Yosemite & other fees.  
6. Map offline navigation on Google Maps & download audiobooks/playlists.  
7. Pack layers, reusable water bottles, sun protection, and a 12-V cooler.

────────────────────────────────
DAY-BY-DAY ITINERARY
────────────────────────────────

DAY 1 – San Francisco ➜ Monterey Peninsula (120 mi)
----------------------------------------------------
Morning  
• Pick up car SFO 08:00; drive south via CA-1.  
• Optional stop: Half Moon Bay coffee/bakery (Granola’s Coffee House).  
Mid-Day  
• Pigeon Point Lighthouse (stretch + photos).  
• Santa Cruz Boardwalk for classic beach vibe OR Mystery Spot 20 min inland.  
Afternoon  
• Arrive Monterey 15:00. Visit world-class Monterey Bay Aquarium (reserve 14:30 entry).  
• Cannery Row stroll, sample clam chowder at Old Fisherman’s Grotto.  
Evening  
• 17-Mile Drive sunset loop through Pebble Beach, Lone Cypress.  
• Overnight in Pacific Grove (Bide-A-Wee Inn or Airbnb cottage).  
Driving: ≈3 h + scenic pull-offs.

DAY 2 – Monterey ➜ Big Sur ➜ San Luis Obispo (145 mi)
----------------------------------------------------
Morning  
• Depart 08:00; quick coffee at Captain + Stoker.  
• MUST-SEE pull-offs: Bixby Bridge, Pfeiffer Beach (purple sand), McWay Falls (Julia Pfeiffer Burns SP).  
• Option: 2-h hike in Andrew Molera SP (Bluffs/Spring Trail loop).  
Mid-Day  
• Lunch: Nepenthe (iconic terrace) or Big Sur Bakery.  
• Continue south; stoppable sights: Limekiln Falls, Gorda seals look-out.  
Afternoon  
• Hearst Castle tour in San Simeon (reserve 16:00 tour).  
• Elephant Seal Vista Point at Piedras Blancas.  
Evening  
• Arrive San Luis Obispo 18:30. Thursday nights: lively farmers’ market downtown.  
• Stay: Madonna Inn (kitschy fun) or SLO Brew Lofts.  
Driving: ≈4 h curves; top up fuel at Big Sur River Inn.

DAY 3 – SLO ➜ Santa Barbara ➜ Pasadena/LA Foothills (185 mi)
------------------------------------------------------------
Morning  
• Coffee & Danish at Scout SLO; on road 08:30.  
• Scenic CA-1 cut through Pismo Beach; quick sand-dune stroll.  
Mid-Day  
• Santa Barbara arrival 11:00; Mission Santa Barbara + Presidio or relaxed beach bike ride.  
• Lunch: Brophy Bros. at harbor (seafood).  
Afternoon  
• Head east on US-101 ➜ CA-134 to Pasadena (avoid downtown LA traffic).  
• Optional detour: Topanga Canyon for Pacific Coast Hwy views.  
Evening  
• Old Pasadena dining scene; book table at Union (hyper-local Italian) or Maestro (modern Mexican).  
• Lodging: The Westin Pasadena or budget-friendly Hotel Dena.  
Driving: ≈3 h + LA traffic cushion.

DAY 4 – Pasadena ➜ Yosemite National Park (290 mi)
--------------------------------------------------
Early Morning  
• Depart 06:00 to beat traffic; I-210 ➜ CA-99 ➜ CA-41 north.  
• Breakfast pit stop in Bakersfield (19th Street Coffee).  
Mid-Day  
• Gas + groceries in Fresno or Oakhurst (cheaper than park).  
• Enter Yosemite South Entrance 12:00ish; stop at Tunnel View for jaw-drop panorama.  
Afternoon  
• Valley highlights loop: Bridalveil Fall, El Cap meadow, Yosemite Falls.  
• 2–3 h hike suggestions: Mist Trail to Vernal Fall footbridge (moderate) or Mirror Lake (easy).  
Evening  
• Sunset at Glacier Point (check seasonal road status).  
• Stay inside park if you scored rooms (Yosemite Valley Lodge) OR drive 40 min to Rush Creek Lodge (Groveland side).  
Driving: ≈5 h total.

DAY 5 – Yosemite ➜ Gold Country ➜ San Francisco (300 mi)
-------------------------------------------------------
Morning  
• Early 07:00 walk in the Valley to avoid crowds; coffee at Degnan’s.  
• Exit via CA-120 (Big Oak Flat Rd).  
Mid-Day  
• Columbia State Historic Park (living-history Gold-Rush town). Pan for gold, grab lunch at Fallon Ice Cream Parlor.  
• Continue west through rolling vineyards of Lodi; possible wine tasting at Michael David Winery.  
Afternoon  
• Cross Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta; Brentwood farm-stand stop (fresh cherries May–Jun).  
Evening  
• Return car SFO 18:00; flight home or one extra night in SF (optional: Alcatraz night tour if staying).  
Driving: ≈5 h.

────────────────────────────────
LODGING SUMMARY
────────────────────────────────
Night 1: Pacific Grove / Monterey  
Night 2: San Luis Obispo  
Night 3: Pasadena (LA area)  
Night 4: Yosemite (inside park or nearby)  

────────────────────────────────
ESTIMATED BUDGET (per couple)
────────────────────────────────
• Rental car (5 days): $425 incl. tax, insurance, toll tag  
• Fuel (1,050 mi @ 28 mpg, $5.50/gal): $205  
• Lodging mid-range: $220 × 4 nights ≈ $880  
• Food & drinks: $120/day × 5 ≈ $600  
• Activities/fees:  
 – Yosemite + other park fees (covered by $80 pass)  
 – Monterey Bay Aquarium $120 (2 adults)  
 – Hearst Castle $60  
 – Misc museum/hike parking $40  
• Souvenirs/margin: $200  
TOTAL ≈ $2,510

────────────────────────────────
OPTIONAL ADD-ONS / ALTERNATES
────────────────────────────────
• Swap LA/Pasadena for Joshua Tree NP (overnight in Palm Springs).  
• Wine-centric variant: spend Day 3 in Santa Ynez Valley tastings, overnight Solvang.  
• Winter version: replace Big Sur (mudslide risk) with inland Paso Robles & hot-springs loop.  

────────────────────────────────
QUICK TIPS & SAFETY
────────────────────────────────
1. Cell service fades along Big Sur and Yosemite—carry offline maps.  
2. Check Caltrans (dot.ca.gov) for Hwy 1 closures and Tioga/Glacier Pt. road status.  
3. Bear-safe food storage rules apply inside Yosemite.  
4. Layered clothing: coastal mornings cool (50 °F) vs. inland afternoons hot (90 °F).  
5. Fill gas when tank <½ in rural stretches; limited stations Big Sur & Yosemite.  
6. Aim weeknight stays for lower hotel rates.  
7. Leave no trace: pack out trash, reusable utensils.  
8. Sunset times: Apr ≈19:40, Jun ≈20:30, Oct ≈18:30.

────────────────────────────────
PACKING SNAPSHOT
────────────────────────────────
• Driver’s license, park pass, printed permits  
• Light puffer jacket + hoodie  
• Hiking shoes + flip-flops  
• Sun hat, SPF 30+, sunglasses  
• Insulated water bottles (2 L pp/day in Yosemite)  
• Small daypack & rain shell  
• Portable phone battery, USB-C/Lightning cables  
• Camera & 128 GB card  
• Snacks: trail mix, fruit, jerky  
• Reusable coffee mug & utensil set  
• Small first-aid & motion-sickness meds (Big Sur curves!)

────────────────────────────────
FINAL WEEK TIMELINE (T-7 to T-0)
────────────────────────────────
T-7 days: Confirm weather, check road advisories, re-verify lodging.  
T-5 days: Online check-ins, download entertainment for flights & drives.  
T-3 days: Pack, print QR tickets, set mail hold.  
T-1 day: Flight, collect rental, overnight SF or start early Day 1.  
T-0: Hit the road—enjoy California!

Have a fantastic adventure!
